iboxs31_camera_init.tooltip: Opens the OV3660 (640×480 RGB565, 20 MHz XCLK, two frame buffers using about 1.2 MB of PSRAM). It can be called again to retry after a failure

iboxs31_camera_ready.tooltip: True once initialization succeeded and frames can be taken

iboxs31_camera_error.tooltip: Why initialization failed, such as no answer or not enough PSRAM; empty on success

iboxs31_camera_flip.tooltip: Flip or mirror the picture in the sensor; later photos and colour coordinates follow it

iboxs31_camera_exposure.tooltip: Target brightness of auto exposure, -5 to +5; 0 is the default, positive is brighter

iboxs31_camera_capture.tooltip: Takes the latest frame and computes brightness and colours (waits up to 0.5 s); true on success. Read them with the picture blocks afterwards

iboxs31_camera_average.tooltip: Average over the whole picture taken last, 0–255

iboxs31_camera_pixel.tooltip: Colour at a point of the picture taken last, 0–255; x 0–639, y 0–479 from the top left, sampled on an 8×8 pixel grid

iboxs31_camera_save_bmp.message0: camera save a photo to SD card %1
iboxs31_camera_save_bmp.tooltip: Takes a photo and saves it as a 24-bit BMP; true on success. Normally 640×480 (about 900 KB); while the video stream runs it uses the stream size. Initialize the card with IBoxS31_SDCard first; writing takes 1–2 s

iboxs31_camera_stream_start.message0: camera start video stream size %1 pixel format %2
iboxs31_camera_stream_start.tooltip: Keeps grabbing the latest picture in the background (turned upright and scaled), about 10 fps, without blocking the program; 320×240 matches the screen. Big-endian matches IBoxS31_Display, little-endian suits TFT_eSPI and LVGL. While it runs, take-a-frame, colour and BMP blocks read from the stream

iboxs31_camera_stream_stop.tooltip: Stops the background capture and frees the stream buffers

iboxs31_camera_stream_new_frame.message0: video stream has a new picture
iboxs31_camera_stream_new_frame.tooltip: True when a new frame is ready; it holds that frame so you can hand "video stream picture data" to a display block right after. The frame stays unchanged until the next check

iboxs31_camera_stream_pixels.tooltip: Pixels of the frame taken last (const uint16_t*, RGB565, row by row from the top left, width×height) for display blocks of other libraries; take a frame with "has a new picture" first

iboxs31_camera_stream_info.tooltip: Picture width and height in pixels, frame rate over the last second, frames since start, and bytes per frame (width×height×2); 0 while the stream is off
